title: Getting started with waveform
text: Let X(t)X(t) mean-zero Gaussian random process. smoothed process can written convolution normalized Gaussian kernel: Y(t)=(X*KσK)(t)=∫−∞∞X(t−u)KσK(u)du,𝔼[X(t)]=0, Y(t) = (X * K_{\sigma_K})(t)      = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} X(t-u) K_{\sigma_K}(u)\,du, \qquad \mathbb{E}[X(t)] = 0, KσK(u)=12πσKexp⁡(−u22σK2). K_{\sigma_K}(u) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}\,\sigma_K} \exp\!\left(-\frac{u^2}{2\sigma_K^2}\right). kernel centered zero, μ=0\mu=0. relationship standard deviation σK\sigma_K full width half maximum FWHM=2σK2ln⁡2⇔σK=FWHM8ln⁡2. \mathrm{FWHM} = 2\sigma_K\sqrt{2\ln 2} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \sigma_K = \frac{\mathrm{FWHM}}{\sqrt{8\ln 2}}. FWHM full width Gaussian kernel half maximum height. package, fwhm supplies width.

title: Getting started with waveform
text: Curve matrices waveform use rows evaluation points columns curves. example, gaussian_swn() returns matrix num_points rows number_of_curves columns.

title: Getting started with waveform
text: Set seed want reproducible random curves. parameters generate five curves 101-point domain. mu requested mean, sig requested standard deviation, fwhm full width half maximum smoothing kernel. Larger fwhm values produce smoother curves. mu sig can single numbers, apply across entire domain every curve, vectors one value per evaluation point. Pointwise vectors shared across curves. example, vectors can specify mean standard deviation change across domain: Plot curves see generated functional data.
code: set.seed(123)  generated <- gaussian_curves_generator(   sample_size = 5,   num_points = 101,   mu = 0,   sig = 1,   fwhm = 20 )  dim(generated$curves) #> [1] 101   5 varying_parameters <- gaussian_curves_generator(   sample_size = 5,   num_points = 101,   mu = seq(-0.5, 0.5, length.out = 101),   sig = seq(0.5, 1.5, length.out = 101),   fwhm = 20 ) dim(varying_parameters$curves) #> [1] 101   5 matplot(   x = 0:(nrow(generated$curves) - 1),   y = generated$curves,   type = "l",   lty = 1,   xlab = "Evaluation point", #can be changed to match your domain   ylab = "Value",   main = "Smoothed Gaussian curves" )

what: Compare smoothness on the same noise
title: Getting started with waveform
text: isolate effect fwhm, generate white noise pass matrix smooth_gaussian_curves() smoothing level. fwhm must positive finite number. Use gaussian_swn() directly get unsmoothed curves; smooth_gaussian_curves() accept fwhm = 0. fwhm becomes large relative domain, smoothed curves approach constant curves.
code: set.seed(123) noise <- gaussian_swn(number_of_curves = 3, num_points = 101)  less_smooth <- smooth_gaussian_curves(noise, mu = 0, sig = 1, fwhm = 5) more_smooth <- smooth_gaussian_curves(noise, mu = 0, sig = 1, fwhm = 20)  par(mfrow = c(1, 2)) matplot(less_smooth, type = "l", lty = 1, main = "FWHM = 5",         xlab = "Evaluation point", ylab = "Value") matplot(more_smooth, type = "l", lty = 1, main = "FWHM = 20",         xlab = "Evaluation point", ylab = "Value") par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

title: Getting started with waveform
text: gaussian_signal(), sin_signal(), cos_signal() return signal values domain. square_signal() returns vector zero-based domain. signals can plotted combined curves.
code: gaussian <- gaussian_signal(   center = 50, amplitude = 2, sfwhm = 12, num_points = 101 ) sine <- sin_signal(   num_points = 101, amplitude = 1, frequency = 0.03, phase = 0, offset = 0 ) cosine <- cos_signal(   num_points = 101, amplitude = 1, frequency = 0.03, phase = 0, offset = 0 ) square <- square_signal(   start_end_signal = c(20, 60), start_height = 0,   signal_height = 1, num_points = 101 )  signal_matrix <- cbind(   Gaussian = gaussian$signal_values,   Sine = sine$signal_values,   Cosine = cosine$signal_values,   Square = square ) matplot(gaussian$domain, signal_matrix, type = "l", lty = 1:4,         xlab = "Evaluation point", ylab = "Value", main = "Signal shapes") legend("topright", legend = colnames(signal_matrix), lty = 1:4)

title: Getting started with waveform
text: estimate_fwhm() estimates residual-field smoothness. observations Yig(t)Y_{ig}(t) group gg, residual functions r̂ig(t)=Yig(t)−μ̂g(t), \hat r_{ig}(t) = Y_{ig}(t) - \hat\mu_g(t), g∈{1,2}g\\{1,2\}, =1,…,ngi=1,\ldots,n_g, μ̂g(t)\hat\mu_g(t) estimated group mean function. point, residual derivative sums squares SSr(t)=∑g∑ir̂ig(t)2,SSr′(t)=∑g∑(r̂ig′(t))2,r̂ig′(t)=dr̂ig(t)dt. SS_{r}(t) = \sum_g \sum_i \hat r_{ig}(t)^2, \qquad SS_{r'}(t) = \sum_g \sum_i \left(\hat r'_{ig}(t)\right)^2, \qquad \hat r'_{ig}(t) = \frac{d\hat r_{ig}(t)}{dt}. local derivative ratio local FWHM λ̂(t)=SSr′(t)SSr(t),FWHM̂(t)=4ln⁡2λ̂(t). \hat\lambda(t) = \frac{SS_{r'}(t)}{SS_{r}(t)}, \qquad \widehat{\mathrm{FWHM}}(t) = \sqrt{\frac{4\ln 2}{\hat\lambda(t)}}. implementation approximates derivatives finite differences unit-spaced domain. reports global estimate reciprocal mean resels per node: FWHM̂=[1|T*|∑t∈T*λ̂(t)4ln⁡2]−1, \widehat{\mathrm{FWHM}} = \left[\frac{1}{|T^*|}\sum_{t\T^*} \sqrt{\frac{\hat\lambda(t)}{4\ln 2}}\right]^{-1}, T*T^* contains points nonzero residual sum squares. Residual smoothness relevant inference one-dimensional trajectories; see Pataky, Vanrenterghem, Robinson (2016) (Pataky et al. 2016). one group, estimate_fwhm() centers supplied curves pointwise. multiple groups, provide residual curves centering within group.
code: estimated_fwhm <- estimate_fwhm(R = generated$curves) estimated_fwhm #> [1] 17.46428

title: Getting started with waveform
text: dense_data() fits curves fda B-spline basis evaluates new grid. new grid can fewer points input grid. output evaluated across domain original curves. following figure compares original, 200-point, 50-point evaluation grids three vertically stacked panels. panel shows five curves domain uses vertical scale.
code: dense_200 <- dense_data(data = generated$curves, num_evaluation = 200) dense_50 <- dense_data(data = generated$curves, num_evaluation = 50) dim(dense_200) #> [1] 200   5 dim(dense_50) #> [1] 50  5 domain_original <- seq(   from = 0,   to = nrow(generated$curves) - 1,   length.out = nrow(generated$curves) ) domain_200 <- seq(   from = 0,   to = nrow(generated$curves) - 1,   length.out = nrow(dense_200) ) domain_50 <- seq(   from = 0,   to = nrow(generated$curves) - 1,   length.out = nrow(dense_50) )  curve_colors <- grDevices::hcl.colors(ncol(generated$curves), "Dark 3") plot_ylim <- range(generated$curves, dense_200, dense_50) par(mfrow = c(3, 1), mar = c(2.5, 4, 2, 1))  matplot(domain_original, generated$curves, type = "b", pch = 16, cex = 0.5,         lty = 1, col = curve_colors, xlim = range(domain_original),         ylim = plot_ylim, xlab = "", ylab = "Value",         main = "Original: 101 points") matplot(domain_200, dense_200, type = "l", lty = 1,         col = curve_colors, xlim = range(domain_original),         ylim = plot_ylim, xlab = "", ylab = "Value",         main = "Dense: 200 points") matplot(domain_50, dense_50, type = "l", lty = 1,         col = curve_colors, xlim = range(domain_original),         ylim = plot_ylim, xlab = "Evaluation point", ylab = "Value",         main = "Sparse: 50 points") par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

title: Getting started with waveform
text: general two-group simulation can written Yig(t)=μ0(t)+δg(t)+ϵig(t), Y_{ig}(t) = \mu_0(t) + \delta_g(t) + \epsilon_{ig}(t), μ0(t)\mu_0(t) baseline signal, δg(t)\delta_g(t) group-specific effect, ϵig(t)\epsilon_{ig}(t) random noise. signal shape, effect pattern, noise standard deviation, noise FWHM can varied build different scenarios.

title: Getting started with waveform
text: Combine Gaussian peak low-amplitude sine component define baseline waveform.
code: practical_num_points <- 101 practical_domain <- seq(0, practical_num_points - 1)  baseline_peak <- gaussian_signal(   center = 45, amplitude = 2, sfwhm = 16,   num_points = practical_num_points ) baseline_oscillation <- sin_signal(   num_points = practical_num_points,   amplitude = 0.25, frequency = 0.02, phase = 0, offset = 0 ) baseline_signal <- baseline_peak$signal_values +   baseline_oscillation$signal_values  plot(practical_domain, baseline_signal, type = "l", lwd = 2,      xlab = "Evaluation point", ylab = "Signal",      main = "Step 1: Baseline signal")

title: Getting started with waveform
text: Combine signals smoothed noise obtain simulated data matrix. Rows evaluation points columns curves.  resulting simulated_data matrix can passed downstream functional analyses.
code: group1_columns <- seq_len(practical_sample_size) group2_columns <- practical_sample_size + seq_len(practical_sample_size)  group1_data <- sweep(   smooth_noise[, group1_columns, drop = FALSE], 1, group1_mean, "+" ) group2_data <- sweep(   smooth_noise[, group2_columns, drop = FALSE], 1, group2_mean, "+" ) simulated_data <- cbind(group1_data, group2_data)  plot(NA, xlim = range(practical_domain),      ylim = range(simulated_data, group1_mean, group2_mean),      xlab = "Evaluation point", ylab = "Observed value",      main = "Step 5: Simulated functional data") matlines(practical_domain, group1_data, col = "steelblue", lty = 1) matlines(practical_domain, group2_data, col = "firebrick", lty = 1) lines(practical_domain, group1_mean, col = "navy", lwd = 3) lines(practical_domain, group2_mean, col = "darkred", lwd = 3) legend("topright",        legend = c("Control curves", "Effect-group curves",                   "Control mean", "Effect-group mean"),        col = c("steelblue", "firebrick", "navy", "darkred"),        lty = 1, lwd = c(1, 1, 3, 3), bty = "n")

what: Example data: thorax obliquity during walking
title: Getting started with waveform
text: package includes two sets functional curves describing thorax obliquity (upward downward trunk motion) walking: male contains curves 65 male participants female contains curves 71 female participants. matrices 101 rows, representing common evaluation grid, one column per participant. data come publicly available full-body gait dataset described Van Criekinge et al. (2023) (Van Criekinge et al. 2023). See ?male ?female details source. following plot overlays participant curves, using color distinguish two groups. horizontal axis indexes 101 points common grid.  observed curves provide example kind functional data want represent simulations. package’s generators let us create curves controlled signals, noise, smoothness simulated data can reflect key characteristics original data.
code: data("male", package = "waveform") data("female", package = "waveform")  evaluation_grid <- seq(0, 100, length.out = 101) male_color <- grDevices::adjustcolor("#2878B5", alpha.f = 0.35) female_color <- grDevices::adjustcolor("#D1495B", alpha.f = 0.35)  matplot(   x = evaluation_grid,   y = male,   type = "l",   lty = 1,   col = male_color,   xlab = "Evaluation point",   ylab = "Thorax obliquity",   main = "Thorax obliquity curves by participant" ) matlines(   x = evaluation_grid,   y = female,   type = "l",   lty = 1,   col = female_color ) legend(   "topright",   legend = c("Male participants", "Female participants"),   col = c("#2878B5", "#D1495B"),   lty = 1,   lwd = 2,   bty = "n" )

text: First, estimate group’s mean function subtract observed curves obtain residuals. Estimate residual FWHM pointwise residual standard deviation separately group. left panel shows group mean functions. right panel shows within-group residual functions subtracting means.
code: residuals_male <- sweep(male, 1, rowMeans(male), FUN = "-") residuals_female <- sweep(female, 1, rowMeans(female), FUN = "-")  fwhm_male <- estimate_fwhm(residuals_male) fwhm_female <- estimate_fwhm(residuals_female)  fwhm_male #> [1] 47.08095 fwhm_female #> [1] 59.08177  sd_male <- apply(residuals_male, 1, sd) sd_female <- apply(residuals_female, 1, sd)  mean_male <- rowMeans(male) mean_female <- rowMeans(female) par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))  matplot(   evaluation_grid, cbind(Male = mean_male, Female = mean_female),   type = "l", lty = 1, lwd = 2, col = c("#2878B5", "#D1495B"),   xlab = "Evaluation point", ylab = "Mean thorax obliquity",   main = "Estimated group means" ) legend("topright", legend = c("Male", "Female"),        col = c("#2878B5", "#D1495B"), lty = 1, lwd = 2, bty = "n")  plot(   NA, xlim = range(evaluation_grid),   ylim = range(residuals_male, residuals_female),   xlab = "Evaluation point", ylab = "Residual thorax obliquity",   main = "Residual functions" ) matlines(evaluation_grid, residuals_male, col =            grDevices::adjustcolor("#2878B5", alpha.f = 0.18), lty = 1) matlines(evaluation_grid, residuals_female, col =            grDevices::adjustcolor("#D1495B", alpha.f = 0.18), lty = 1) legend("topright", legend = c("Male", "Female"),        col = c("#2878B5", "#D1495B"), lty = 1, lwd = 2, bty = "n") par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

title: Estimate the FWHM of a residual random field — estimate_fwhm
text: evaluation point t, local derivative ratio lambda(t) = SS[r_derivative(t)] / SS[r(t)], sums squares taken across curves. local FWHM sqrt(4 * log(2) / lambda(t)). returned global estimate reciprocal mean resels per node, 1 / mean(sqrt(lambda(t) / (4 * log(2)))), points nonzero residual sum squares.

title: Estimate the FWHM of a residual random field — estimate_fwhm
